FNH 160.title: Integrated Physiology for Human Nutrition I
FNH 160.description: Basic principles in human physiology, including function of the nervous, endocrine, musculoskeletal and digestive systems, integration across systems, maintenance of homeostasis, and application to human nutrition.
FNH 160.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 11, CHEM 12, CHEM 100, CHEM 110, CHEM 111 and one of BIOL 11, ATPH 12, BIOL 12, BIOL 111. FNH 160 and 161 together are credit-excluded with BIOL 153 and 155

FNH 161.title: Integrated Physiology for Human Nutrition II
FNH 161.description: Basic principles in human physiology, including function of the cardiovascular, immune, respiratory, urinary and reproductive systems, integration across systems, maintenance of homeostasis, and application to human nutrition.
FNH 161.prerequisiteText: FNH 160. FNH 160 and 161 together are credit-excluded with BIOL 153 and 155

FNH 200.title: Exploring Our Food
FNH 200.description: Chemical and physical properties of foods; issues pertaining to safety, nutritive value and consumer acceptability; government regulations pertaining to food safety, quality and additives; preservation techniques and transformation of agricultural commodities to food products; foods of the future.

prerequisite.raw: At least second year standing required

FNH 200.prerequisiteText: At least second year standing required

FNH 250.title: Nutrition Concepts and Controversies
FNH 250.description: Fundamental concepts and principles of human nutrition applied to current nutrition issues.
FNH 250.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of FNH 160, FNH 161 or (b) one of BIOL 111, BIOL 112, BIOL 153, BIOL 155 or (c) all of KIN 131, KIN 132. At least second-year standing required

FNH 290.title: Introductory Topics in Food, Nutrition, and Health
FNH 290.description: Analysis and interpretation of current issues in food, nutrition, and health. Topics will vary from year to year.

FNH 300.title: Food Engineering
FNH 300.description: Units and dimensions, mass balance, energy balance, steady state and transient heat flow, fluid handling and measurement.
FNH 300.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 170

FNH 301.title: Food Chemistry
FNH 301.description: Chemical and physical properties and reactions of food constituents, including water, carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, minerals and vitamins.

FNH 302.title: Food Analysis
FNH 302.description: Principles of and procedures for analysis of the chemical and physical properties of food; proximate analysis; introduction to instrumental analysis; reporting and analysis of data.
FNH 302.prerequisiteText: Either (a) CHEM_V 205, (b) CHEM_V 210, or (c) CHEM_V 211; and either (a) CHEM_V 203 or (b) CHEM_V 233

FNH 303.title: Food Product Development
FNH 303.description: Introduction to and application of concepts involved in food product formulation and development.
FNH 303.prerequisiteText: One of LFS 252, BIOL 300, EPSE 482, FRST 231, STAT 200

FNH 309.title: Food Processing
FNH 309.description: Preservation of tissue and fluid food systems by selected physical and chemical treatments with emphasis on product-process interactions.
FNH 309.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 12, PHYS 100, PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 170

FNH 313.title: Food Microbiology
FNH 313.description: Roles of microorganisms in food production, preservation, spoilage, and foodborne disease; factors affecting growth, survival and inactivation of microorganisms in foods; methods for identifying, enumerating, and eliminating microorganisms in food-production environments.

FNH 325.title: Food Science Laboratory I
FNH 325.description: Laboratory techniques used in food chemistry, microbiology and processing; statistical analysis and presentation of experimental data; scientific report writing. Enrolment restricted to Food Science students.

FNH 326.title: Food Science Laboratory II
FNH 326.description: Laboratory techniques used in food analysis, food processing, sensory science and product development; statistical analysis and presentation of experimental data; scientific report writing. Enrolment restricted to Food Science students.

FNH 330.title: Introduction to Wine Science I
FNH 330.description: Principles of viticulture, enology, and wine microbiology and chemistry; marketing, regulation and classification of wines from selected regions of the world; social, economic and health aspects of wine consumption; wine appreciation.

FNH 335.title: Introduction to Wine Science II
FNH 335.description: Review of diverse styles of wine with consideration of classic wine-producing areas. Concepts in wine microbiology/chemistry; overview of steps in grape processing for diverse wine styles. Comparison of regulations for Canadian VQA systems with international systems. Wine sensory analysis.
FNH 335.prerequisiteText: FNH 330. and third-year standing or higher

FNH 340.title: Food Theory and Applications
FNH 340.description: Principles of food preparation based on the physical and chemical properties of food, and experimental and practical applications to food preparation.
FNH 340.prerequisiteText: FNH_V 200 and either (a) all of CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 113 or (b) all of CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 123

FNH 342.title: Critical Perspectives on Consumer Food Practices
FNH 342.description: Personal, collective, and policy factors affecting food choices, including perceptions of healthy eating, gender, identity, family structures, and economic, sociocultural, and political forces.

prerequisite.raw: At least third year standing required

FNH 342.prerequisiteText: At least third year standing required

FNH 345.title: Counselling Skills in Dietetics
FNH 345.description: Counselling in dietetics: communication theory and foundational counselling skills.

FNH 350.title: Fundamentals of Nutrition
FNH 350.description: Fundamentals of energy and macronutrient metabolism.
FNH 350.prerequisiteText: FNH_V 250 and one of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203

FNH 351.title: Vitamins, Minerals, and Health
FNH 351.description: Vitamin and mineral nutrition and their role in maintaining and promoting health.
FNH 351.prerequisiteText: FNH_V 250 and one of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203

FNH 355.title: International Nutrition
FNH 355.description: Conceptualization and scientific analyses of global problems in food and nutrition; complexities of food habits and malnutrition in various cultures around the world.

FNH 370.title: Nutrition Assessment
FNH 370.description: The use of dietary, anthropometric, biochemical, and related information for the assessment of nutritional status of individuals and populations.

FNH 371.title: Human Nutrition Over The Life Span
FNH 371.description: Nutritional requirements and dietary patterns of healthy individuals throughout the life span.

FNH 375.title: Nutrition Care I
FNH 375.description: Fundamentals of nutrition care: the nutrition care process (NCP), documentation, nutritional risk and nutritional status assessment, metabolic stress, supplements, pharmacology, and body weight. NCP applied to food allergies and intolerances, gastrointestinal symptoms. Introduction to chronic diseases. Restricted to students in year 3 of the dietetics major.
FNH 375.prerequisiteText: All of FNH_V 350, FNH_V 370 and either (a) one of BIOL_V 153, BIOL_V 155, CAPS_V 301 or (b) all of FNH_V 160 and FNH_V 161

FNH 380.title: Professional Dietetic Practice I
FNH 380.description: Introduction to the profession of dietetics in Canada. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing in the Dietetics Major

FNH 380.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing in the Dietetics Major

FNH 381.title: Dietetics Practice Education Placement I
FNH 381.description: Practice education placements in settings across British Columbia. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major.

FNH 398.title: Research Methods in Human Nutrition
FNH 398.description: Process of research; principles and processes in utilizing research. Restricted to students in majors in the FNH program.
FNH 398.prerequisiteText: FNH 250 and either (a) LFS 252 or (b) BIOL 300 or (c) EPSE 482 or (d) FRST 231 or (e) STAT 200

FNH 401.title: Advances in Plant and Cell-Based Foods
FNH 401.description: Examination of meat, egg, fish, and dairy analogues made using plants, recombinant proteins, and cell cultures, from the molecular to the macroscopic level. Relation of molecular details to physical and sensory properties. Health and sustainability impacts.
FNH 401.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203, CHEM_V 203 or CHEM_V 233. 3rd-year standing or higher

FNH 402.title: Functional Foods
FNH 402.description: Functional food concepts related to efficacy and safety; examples of bioactive component-disease relationships; natural health products; approval of functional food and health claims; the importance of clinical studies in support of efficacy for health claims; market determinants of functional foods.
FNH 402.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203, and third-year standing

FNH 403.title: Food Laws, Regulations and Quality Assurance
FNH 403.description: Canadian and international laws governing food composition, grading, quality and safety; hazard analysis critical control points; statistical quality assurance.
FNH 403.prerequisiteText: One of LFS_V 252, STAT_V 200, FRST_V 231, BIOL_V 300, EPSE_V 482, or equivalent background in statistics

FNH 404.title: Food Safety and Quality Management
FNH 404.description: Food production plant sanitation, environmental monitoring, global food safety standards, and food plant internal audits.

FNH 405.title: Microbiology of Food and Beverage Fermentation
FNH 405.description: Fermentation methods, mechanism and microbiology of nonalcoholic fermented foods and alcoholic fermented beverages (beer, cider, sake).
FNH 405.prerequisiteText: One of MICB_V 211, MICB_V 212, BIOL_V 201, BIOL_V 203, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203. Third-year standing

FNH 413.title: Food Safety
FNH 413.description: Microbial and chemical factors that underlie public health challenges in the food supply chain; prevalence and nature of organisms which cause foodborne diseases; approaches and technologies for improvement of food safety.
FNH 413.prerequisiteText: One of MICB_V 211, MICB_V 212, CHEM_V 233, FNH_V 313

FNH 414.title: Sustainability in the Food Industry
FNH 414.description: Regenerative sustainability and the sustainability nexus; health and environmental impacts of the food industry; environmental performance indicators and management systems; approaches to enhance sustainability in the food industry.

FNH 415.title: Business Concepts in Food, Nutrition, and Health
FNH 415.description: Introduction to and application of business activities in food, nutrition, and health settings.

prerequisite.raw: At least third-year standing in the Faculty of Land and Food Systems

FNH 415.prerequisiteText: At least third-year standing in the Faculty of Land and Food Systems

FNH 419.title: Interfacial Phenomena
FNH 419.description: Outline of the physics and chemistry of interfaces; discussion of the part played by surface effects in technical processes.

FNH 425.title: Food Science Laboratory III
FNH 425.description: Integrated course designed to illustrate principles of research and product development in the food industry.

FNH 430.title: Enology and Wine Biotechnology
FNH 430.description: Yeasts and bacteria involved in wine making, metabolic pathways leading to the production of flavour and spoilage compounds, genetic improvement of wine yeasts, and red and white wine fermentations. Approaches and technologies for the improvement of wine safety. Sensory evaluation of wines.
FNH 430.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 335, MICB 325, FNH 313, BIOC 302

FNH 436.title: Integrated Functional Genomics
FNH 436.description: Global transcript, protein and metabolite profiling technologies, their integration, application, and furtherance of our understanding of how higher organisms function in general.

FNH 440.title: Food Service Systems Management
FNH 440.description: Management responsibilities in quantity food production with emphasis on menu planning, purchasing and service. Includes planning and equipping food services. Restricted to students in the Dietetics major. Note: Course registrants are required to possess a Foodsafe II certificate.

FNH 451.title: Nutrient Metabolism and Implications for Health
FNH 451.description: Integration of nutrient and energy metabolism on a whole-body and individual tissue basis and the implication for health. Emphasis will be on regulation of nutrient metabolism.
FNH 451.prerequisiteText: FNH_V 350, one of BIOC_V 302 or BIOC_V 303, and either (a) one of BIOL_V 153, BIOL_V 155, CAPS_V 301 or (b) all of FNH_V 160 and FNH_V 161

FNH 454.title: Fish Nutrition
FNH 454.description: Physiology of digestion and excretion, nutrient requirements, sources of nutrients, diet formulation, feeding management.

FNH 455.title: Applied International Nutrition
FNH 455.description: Applying nutrition concepts and principles in addressing problems of malnutrition and food insecurity in international settings. Basics of developing culturally acceptable, sustainable nutrition intervention programs.

FNH 470.title: Nutrition Care II
FNH 470.description: Enteral nutrition, parenteral nutrition, and the nutrition care process are applied to select diseases or conditions, including trauma, surgery, critical care, respiratory diseases, gastrointestinal diseases, liver diseases, and diseases of the gallbladder and exocrine pancreas. Restricted to students in year 4 of the dietetics major.

FNH 472.title: Maternal and Fetal Nutrition
FNH 472.description: Metabolic adaptations, nutrient metabolism, and special issues during pregnancy that may influence the maternal-fetal nutritional supply.

FNH 473.title: Applied Public Health Nutrition
FNH 473.description: Theory and methods in public health nutrition and health promotion program planning to assess, plan, implement, and evaluate nutrition-related programs for communities and populations. Considers factors affecting behavior and the social determinants of health.

FNH 474.title: Sport Nutrition
FNH 474.description: Nutritional needs of athletes, including energy, carbohydrate and protein; hydration; pre-and post-event nutrition, weight management and body composition issues; ergogenic aids; sports-specific guidelines; and special athlete populations.

FNH 475.title: Nutrition Care III
FNH 475.description: Nutrition care process applied to select diseases and conditions including dysphagia, cancer, neurological conditions, metabolic syndrome, eating disorders, cardiovascular diseases, endocrine diseases, and renal diseases. Restricted to students in year 4 of the dietetics major.

FNH 477.title: Nutrition and Disease Prevention
FNH 477.description: Evidence-based examination of the role of nutrition in the prevention of chronic disease.

FNH 480.title: Professional Dietetic Practice II
FNH 480.description: Skill development and application for practice education placements and dietetic practice settings. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major.

FNH 481.title: Dietetics Practice Education Placement II
FNH 481.description: Practice education placements in settings across British Columbia. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major. Pass/Fail.

FNH 482.title: Dietetics Practice Education Placement III
FNH 482.description: Practice education placements in settings across British Columbia. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major. Pass/Fail.

FNH 483.title: Dietetics Practice Education Placement IV
FNH 483.description: Practice education placements in settings across British Columbia. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major. Pass/Fail.

FNH 490.title: Advanced Topics in Food, Nutrition, and Health
FNH 490.description: Analysis and interpretation of current issues in food, nutrition and health.

FNH 497.title: Directed Studies in Food, Nutrition and Health

FNH 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
FNH 499.description: Design and execution of an experimental/analytical research project leading to preparation of a thesis.

children.raw: consult before the end of classes in third year

FNH 499.prerequisiteText: Approval of a program advisor; consult before the end of classes in third year
